weekSubtitle: Habitats on Earth (Land Habitats, Forests, Tundra, Freshwater & Oceans)

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Garden, Desert & Savanna
lessons.description: Explore the Home Garden, Desert plants and reptiles, and the Savanna tropical grassland!
lessons.hint: Look at how much rain each habitat gets and how plants and animals survive there!

cards.frontHint: Every living thing has a special home!
cards.explanation: A habitat is the natural home where a plant or animal lives and gets food, water, air, and shelter to survive.
cards.example: Each animal lives in a habitat that gives it food, water, and shelter.
cards.tip: Think of a habitat like a neighborhood built just right for the plants and animals living there!

cards.explanation: Many kinds of insects, such as bees, beetles, and butterflies, live in a home garden. There may also be snails and larger animals like rabbits and mice. Some animals live underground too!
cards.example: Bees, butterflies, snails, rabbits, and mice live in a sunny home garden.
cards.tip: Check both above the flowers AND underground — worms and mice dig cozy burrows!

cards.explanation: A desert is a dry habitat that gets very little rainfall. Some deserts are very hot, while others are hot during the day and cold at night. Because there is not much water, few plants and animals live there.
cards.example: A desert is a dry habitat with very little rainfall and few plants.
cards.tip: Desert plants can survive for a long time without water!

cards.explanation: Desert plants survive with very little water. Some have long roots to reach water deep underground, others have roots that spread out wide, and some store water right inside their stems!
cards.example: Some desert plants use long roots or store water in their thick stems.
cards.tip: Flora means plants! Remember 3 desert plant tricks: deep roots, wide roots, or water-storing stems!

cards.explanation: Reptiles such as snakes, lizards, and tortoises live in deserts. Desert animals can survive with little water, and many get the water they need by eating plants!
cards.example: Snakes, lizards, and tortoises survive in the desert with very little water.
cards.tip: Fauna means animals! Eating juicy desert plants gives desert animals both food and water!

cards.explanation: A savanna, also called a tropical grassland, is a habitat that is hot and dry for most of the year. It has large areas of grasses, small shrubs, and scattered trees.
cards.example: A savanna is a hot and dry tropical grassland with tall grasses and scattered trees.
cards.tip: Savanna = tropical grassland: mostly grass with only a few scattered trees!

cards.explanation: Savanna animals include elephants, giraffes, zebras, wildebeests, lions, and a variety of birds!
cards.example: Elephants, giraffes, zebras, wildebeests, and lions live on the sunny savanna.
cards.tip: Picture a sunny safari with giraffes nibbling tree tops and zebras eating tall grass!

cards.explanation: Many animals in a savanna get food and water by eating plants. When it rains, large waterholes form in the ground and attract lots of animals!
cards.example: When it rains on the savanna, animals gather at large waterholes in the ground.
cards.tip: During dry days, plants give moisture; when rain falls, waterholes fill up like giant puddles!

activity.title: Garden, Desert & Savanna Match!
activity.instruction: Tap a Habitat or Clue on the left, then tap its matching answer on the right!
allPairs: Dry habitat with very little rainfall
Long roots, wide roots, or water in stems
Snakes, lizards, tortoises eating plants for water
Tropical grassland with grasses & scattered trees
Large rain pools in the ground attracting animals
Animals in the garden that burrow below soil

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Rainforests, Forests & Tundra
lessons.description: Compare warm, rainy Tropical Rainforests, cozy Temperate Forests, and snowy Tundra!
lessons.hint: Notice which land habitat is the most diverse, which has tree hollows, and which is a cold treeless plain!

cards.explanation: A tropical rainforest gets lots of rain and sunlight and stays warm all year round. It is the most diverse land habitat on Earth! Even though rainforests cover less than three percent of Earth's surface, they hold more than half of Earth's land animals!
cards.example: A tropical rainforest gets lots of rain and sunlight and is the most diverse land habitat.
cards.tip: Less than 3% of Earth's surface — yet MORE than half of all land animals live there!

cards.explanation: Many kinds of plants grow in every part of a rainforest: tall trees of all shapes and sizes, shrubs, ferns, and mosses. Mosses and small plants even grow on rocks, tree trunks, and logs!
cards.example: Tall trees, shrubs, ferns, and mosses grow on rocks, trunks, and logs.
cards.tip: Look up and look down: tall trees tower overhead while ferns and mosses hug logs below!

cards.explanation: The huge variety of rainforest plants provides food and shelter for many animals, including birds, snakes, frogs, insects, and both large and small mammals!
cards.example: Birds, snakes, frogs, insects, and mammals find food and shelter in the rainforest.
cards.tip: More plant variety means more food and hiding places for every kind of animal!

cards.explanation: A temperate forest has many plants and trees that give lots of food and places for animals to live. Hollows inside tree trunks provide safe shelter for many types of birds!
cards.example: Hollows in temperate forest trees provide shelter for many types of birds.
cards.tip: Look inside old tree trunks — woodpeckers and owls love cozy tree hollows!

cards.explanation: Animals living in a temperate forest include squirrels, raccoons, bears, deer, and many types of birds nesting in tree hollows.
cards.example: Squirrels, raccoons, bears, and deer live among the trees in a temperate forest.
cards.tip: Think of acorns and leafy woods: squirrels, raccoons, bears, and deer belong here!

cards.explanation: A tundra is cold all year round with very little rain and strong winds, and snow or ice covers the ground most of the year. The word tundra comes from a Finnish word meaning 'treeless plain' — few trees grow, mostly grasses and small shrubs that bloom with colorful wildflowers in warmer spring and summer months!
cards.example: A cold, windy tundra has snow most of the year and colorful summer wildflowers.
cards.tip: Tundra = Finnish 'tunturi' (treeless plain)! Few trees, low shrubs, summer wildflowers!

cards.explanation: Not many animals can survive the cold, dry tundra. Animals there include polar bears, reindeer, foxes, and hares. During winter, many tundra animals move underground to stay warm or travel to warmer places!
cards.example: Polar bears, reindeer, foxes, and hares live in the cold tundra habitat.
cards.tip: Winter survival tip in the tundra: go underground to keep warm OR migrate to warmer places!

activity.title: Forest & Tundra Detective!
activity.instruction: Read each habitat clue and tap the best answer!

items.prompt: Which habitat gets lots of rain and sunlight, stays warm all year, and is the MOST diverse land habitat on Earth?
items.targetText: Covers < 3% of Earth, holds > half of land animals!
items.explanation: Tropical rainforests are warm and rainy all year and are the most diverse land habitat on Earth!

items.prompt: Where do squirrels, raccoons, bears, deer, and birds sheltering in tree hollows live?
items.explanation: Temperate forests are home to squirrels, raccoons, bears, deer, and birds nesting in tree hollows!

items.prompt: What is a 'treeless plain' that is cold all year with little rain, snow/ice most of the year, and summer wildflowers?
items.explanation: Tundra comes from 'tunturi' (treeless plain) — cold and windy with grasses, shrubs, and summer wildflowers!

items.prompt: How do many tundra animals survive the freezing winter?
items.targetText: When winter gets icy in the tundra...
options: Move underground to stay warm or move to warmer places
items.answer: Move underground to stay warm or move to warmer places
items.explanation: During winter, many tundra animals burrow underground to keep warm or move to warmer places!

items.prompt: In a tropical rainforest, what grows right on rocks, tree trunks, and logs?
items.explanation: Besides tall trees, shrubs, and ferns, mosses and other small plants grow on rocks, tree trunks, and logs!

items.prompt: Which group of animals can survive in the tundra?
options: Polar bears, reindeer, foxes, and hares
items.answer: Polar bears, reindeer, foxes, and hares
items.explanation: Polar bears, reindeer, arctic foxes, and hares are tundra animals!

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Freshwater, Wetlands & Oceans
lessons.description: Dive into Ponds & Lakes, Rivers & Streams, Wetlands, and Saltwater Oceans (Gills vs. Lungs)!
lessons.hint: Notice which water habitats have fresh water vs. salt water, and how ocean animals breathe!

cards.explanation: Ponds and lakes are closed freshwater habitats. Plants grow in the land around the water, on top of the water, and under the water! Surrounding flowers attract insects and small animals.
cards.example: Ponds and lakes are closed freshwater habitats with plants around, on, and under water.
cards.tip: Closed freshwater means the water stays in one basin like a big bowl (instead of flowing like a river)!

cards.explanation: Common pond and lake animals include turtles, frogs, and birds, plus reptiles like lizards and snakes. Animals live near, on, or under the water!
cards.example: Turtles, frogs, birds, lizards, and snakes live near or in pond water.
cards.tip: Picture a turtle on a log, a frog on a lily pad, and fish swimming underneath!

cards.explanation: Rivers and streams are freshwater habitats where water moves from one place to another. Trees, shrubs, and grasses take in water through roots in the wet soil. Animals include fish, reptiles, mammals, and birds — even the Amazon river dolphin!
cards.example: In rivers and streams, freshwater moves from one place to another.
cards.tip: Fun fact: the pink Amazon river dolphin lives in freshwater rivers instead of the ocean!

cards.explanation: A wetland is a habitat flooded with water for all or most of the year. Some wetlands have fresh water and some have salt water! Wet-season plants include grasses, shrubs, and small trees, and animals include insects, fish, amphibians, reptiles, and mammals.
cards.example: A wetland is flooded with fresh or salt water for most of the year.
cards.tip: Wet + land = land soaked or flooded by water almost all year!

cards.frontHint: What happens to plants and animals?
cards.explanation: When the water amount changes, wetland plants and animals change too! Some plants may die during dry times and grow back when water returns, while animals move to wetter spots, hide in mud, or wait for rain!
cards.example: If a wetland dries up, plants grow back and animals return when water comes back.
cards.tip: Even if a wetland dries for a while, seeds and burrows help life bounce back with the rain!

cards.explanation: The ocean is a very large body of salt water. Oceans are the largest habitat on Earth and cover most of Earth's surface! Unlike rivers and lakes, ocean water is salty and huge.
cards.example: The ocean is a huge body of salt water and the largest habitat on Earth.
cards.tip: Remember: Lakes/Rivers = freshwater; Oceans = SALT water & cover most of Earth!

cards.frontHint: Do all ocean parts feel the same?
cards.explanation: Ocean habitats differ in many ways! Some parts are shallow and have warm water, while deep ocean habitats are cold all year round. Different animals live in different parts of the ocean.
cards.example: Shallow ocean parts can be warm, while deep ocean habitats stay cold all year.
cards.tip: Sunlight warms shallow water near the top; way down deep it stays dark and cold!

cards.frontHint: How do fish vs. dolphins breathe?
cards.explanation: Fish, like most ocean animals, have gills to get the air they need directly from water. Other ocean animals — like dolphins, whales, and turtles — have lungs and swim to the surface to breathe air!
cards.example: Fish use gills to breathe under water, while whales and dolphins surface with lungs.
cards.tip: Fish = Gills (breathe underwater). Dolphins, whales & turtles = Lungs (come up for air)!

activity.title: Splash! Water Habitat Explorer!
activity.instruction: Read each water habitat clue and pick the best answer!

items.prompt: Which habitat is a very large body of salt water that covers most of Earth's surface?
items.explanation: Oceans are huge bodies of salt water and are the largest habitat on Earth!

items.prompt: Whales, dolphins, and sea turtles come to the top of the ocean to breathe air because they have ___.
items.explanation: Dolphins, whales, and turtles have lungs and come to the surface to breathe in air!

items.prompt: How do fish get the air they need right out of the water?
items.explanation: Fish have gills to get the air they need directly from the water!

items.prompt: Which freshwater habitats have water that MOVES from one place to another?
items.targetText: Home to the Amazon river dolphin!
items.explanation: In rivers and streams, fresh water moves from one place to another!

items.prompt: Ponds and lakes are ___ freshwater habitats where turtles, frogs, and water plants live.
items.explanation: Ponds and lakes are closed freshwater habitats!

items.prompt: Which habitat is flooded with water for all or most of the year (either fresh or salt water)?
items.targetText: Changes between wet and dry seasons!
items.explanation: A wetland is flooded with fresh or salt water for all or most of the year!

practices.title: Practice 1: Garden, Desert & Savanna
practices.description: Practice insects and animals in the Home Garden, Desert plants & reptiles, and Savanna grasslands & waterholes!
practices.hint: Garden = bees, snails, rabbits; Desert = very dry, long roots/water stems, reptiles; Savanna = hot grassland with scattered trees & waterholes!

practices.title: Practice 2: Rainforests, Forests & Tundra
practices.description: Practice Tropical Rainforests (most diverse!), Temperate Forests (tree hollows), and Cold Windy Tundra!
practices.hint: Rainforest = warm, wet, ferns & mosses; Temperate forest = bears, deer, squirrels & tree hollows; Tundra = cold treeless plain!

practices.title: Practice 3: Ponds, Rivers, Wetlands & Oceans
practices.description: Practice closed Ponds & Lakes, moving Rivers & Streams, flooded Wetlands, and Oceans (Gills vs. Lungs)!
practices.hint: Freshwater = ponds, lakes, rivers, streams. Salt water = oceans (fish use gills; dolphins/whales use lungs!).

quiz.title: Week 1 Final Quiz: Earth's Habitats
quiz.description: A fun 10-question Science quiz mixing Garden, Desert, Savanna, Rainforest, Temperate Forest, Tundra, Freshwater, Wetlands, and Oceans!
quiz.hint: Think about the weather, water, plants (flora), and animals (fauna) in each habitat!
quiz.instruction: Read the science question and tap the best answer!

questions.instruction: Think about animals in a home garden.
questions.text: Which insects might you spot flying among flowers in a home garden?
questions.answer: Bees, beetles, and butterflies
questions.hint: Think of tiny buzzing and fluttering garden insects!
questions.explanation: Many insects — such as bees, beetles, and butterflies — live in a home garden!

questions.instruction: Remember larger animals and underground dwellers in a garden.
questions.text: Besides insects and snails, which larger animals can live in or under a home garden?
questions.answer: Rabbits and mice (some living underground)
questions.hint: Think of furry hoppers and tiny burrowers near the garden plants!
questions.explanation: Rabbits and mice live in gardens too, and some garden animals live underground!

questions.instruction: Remember what a desert is like.
questions.text: Which sentence best describes a desert habitat?
options: It is dry and gets very little rainfall
It gets heavy rain every single day
It is flooded with water all year long
It is covered with ice and snow all year
questions.answer: It is dry and gets very little rainfall
questions.hint: Think of sunny sand, cactuses, and almost no rain!
questions.explanation: A desert is a dry habitat that gets very little rainfall!

questions.instruction: Think about temperature in different deserts.
questions.text: How can temperatures change from day to night in some deserts?
options: Hot during the day and cold during the night
Always freezing snowy ice both day and night
questions.answer: Hot during the day and cold during the night
questions.hint: Our desert card explains: Some deserts are very hot, while others change between daytime and nighttime!
questions.explanation: Some deserts are hot during the day and become cold during the night!

questions.instruction: Look at how desert plants (Flora) survive.
questions.text: How do desert plants get and keep the water they need?
options: They have long deep roots, spread-out roots, or store water in their stems
They absorb melted snow on frozen ice
They have gills to breathe underwater
questions.answer: They have long deep roots, spread-out roots, or store water in their stems
questions.hint: Think about a cactus stem and long underground roots!
questions.explanation: Desert plants reach water with long or wide-spreading roots, and plants like cactuses store water in their stems!

questions.instruction: Look at desert animals (Fauna).
questions.text: Which group of reptiles can be found in desert habitats?
questions.answer: Snakes, lizards, and tortoises
questions.hint: Remember the desert Fauna card: scaly reptiles that survive with little water!
questions.explanation: Reptiles such as snakes, lizards, and tortoises live in deserts!

questions.instruction: Think about how desert animals get water.
questions.text: When there are no ponds nearby, how do many desert animals get the water they need?
questions.answer: By eating plants
questions.hint: Juicy desert plants hold stored water inside them!
questions.explanation: Many desert animals get the water they need by eating plants!

questions.instruction: Identify the Savanna habitat.
questions.text: A savanna is also called a ___ that is hot and dry for most of the year.
questions.answer: tropical grassland
questions.hint: Notice it has large areas of grass!
questions.explanation: A savanna, also called a tropical grassland, is hot and dry for most of the year!

questions.instruction: Think about plants growing on a savanna.
questions.text: What kinds of plants grow across a savanna habitat?
options: Large areas of grasses, small shrubs, and scattered trees
Lily pads floating under a pond
Only tall rainforest ferns in heavy daily rain
questions.answer: Large areas of grasses, small shrubs, and scattered trees
questions.hint: Not crowded like a thick forest — lots of grass with trees spread apart!
questions.explanation: A savanna has large areas of grasses, small shrubs, and scattered trees!

questions.instruction: Spot savanna animals (Fauna).
questions.text: Which set of animals lives together in a savanna habitat?
options: Elephants, giraffes, zebras, wildebeests, and lions
Polar bears, hares, and arctic foxes
questions.answer: Elephants, giraffes, zebras, wildebeests, and lions
questions.hint: Think of tall-necked leaf-eaters and striped grass-eaters near a waterhole!
questions.explanation: Elephants, giraffes, zebras, wildebeests, lions, and many birds live in a savanna!

questions.instruction: Remember what happens when it rains on the savanna.
questions.text: When it rains in a savanna, what attracts many animals to drink?
options: Large waterholes that form in the ground
Hollows high up in oak trees
questions.answer: Large waterholes that form in the ground
questions.hint: Elephants, zebras, and giraffes gather around these big rain pools!
questions.explanation: When it rains, savanna animals are attracted to large waterholes that form in the ground!

questions.instruction: Compare desert plants and waterholes.
questions.text: Why can only a FEW plants and animals live in deserts?
options: Because there is not much water in the desert
Because deserts get flooded by oceans every week
Because desert trees grow too tall and block the sun
Because deserts have too many rushing rivers
questions.answer: Because there is not much water in the desert
questions.hint: All living things need water, and deserts get very little rainfall!
questions.explanation: With not much water available, only few specially adapted plants and animals can live in deserts!

questions.instruction: Compare garden and savanna.
questions.text: Where would you find bees and butterflies pollinating flowers right outside a house?
questions.answer: A home garden habitat
questions.hint: Look at our Home Garden animal card with a bunny, snail, and butterflies!
questions.explanation: Insects like bees, beetles, and butterflies live right in a home garden habitat!

questions.instruction: Spot the false claim about deserts.
questions.text: Which statement about DESERT plants is TRUE?
options: Desert plants can survive for a long time without water
Desert plants must be flooded underwater all year
Desert plants only bloom under snow
questions.answer: Desert plants can survive for a long time without water
questions.hint: Cactuses store water inside their stems for dry days!
questions.explanation: Desert plants can survive a long time without water using deep/wide roots and water-storing stems!

questions.instruction: Compare savanna food & water sources.
questions.text: Many savanna animals get BOTH food and water by eating ___.
questions.answer: plants
questions.hint: Plants contain both nutrients and moisture!
questions.explanation: Many animals in a savanna get the food and water they need by eating plants!

questions.instruction: Think about weather in a Tropical Rainforest.
questions.text: What is the weather like in a tropical rainforest?
options: Lots of rain and sunlight, and warm all year round
Dry with almost no rain all year
Covered in snow and ice all year
Cold and windy with no trees
questions.answer: Lots of rain and sunlight, and warm all year round
questions.hint: Why is it called a TROPICAL RAIN-forest?
questions.explanation: A tropical rainforest gets lots of rain and sunlight and stays warm all year round!

questions.instruction: Remember this Amazing Fact about Tropical Rainforests!
questions.text: Which land habitat is the MOST DIVERSE land habitat on Earth?
questions.answer: Tropical rainforest
questions.hint: Even though it covers under 3% of Earth's surface, more than half of Earth's land animals live here!
questions.explanation: Tropical rainforests are the most diverse land habitat on Earth!

questions.instruction: Remember the Tropical Rainforest Amazing Fact numbers!
questions.text: Tropical rainforests cover less than 3% of Earth's surface, yet are home to ___.
options: more than half of Earth's land animals
questions.answer: more than half of Earth's land animals
questions.hint: Think how crowded with life rainforests are — more than 50% of land animals!
questions.explanation: Even though they cover less than 3% of Earth's surface, tropical rainforests hold more than half of Earth's land animals!

questions.instruction: Look at Tropical Rainforest plants.
questions.text: In a rainforest, mosses and other small plants grow right on ___.
questions.answer: rocks, tree trunks, and logs
questions.hint: Think of soft green moss hugging damp forest surfaces!
questions.explanation: Alongside tall trees, shrubs, and ferns, mosses and small plants grow on rocks, tree trunks, and logs!

questions.instruction: Identify plants in a Tropical Rainforest.
questions.text: Which group lists plants found in a tropical rainforest?
options: Tall trees, shrubs, ferns, and mosses
questions.answer: Tall trees, shrubs, ferns, and mosses
questions.hint: Rainforests have layers of plants from tall canopy trees down to leafy ferns and soft mosses!
questions.explanation: Tropical rainforests have tall trees of all shapes and sizes, shrubs, ferns, and mosses!

questions.instruction: Notice why so many animals live in a rainforest.
questions.text: Why can so many birds, snakes, frogs, insects, and mammals live in a tropical rainforest?
options: The great diversity of plants gives them lots of food and shelter
Because there are no plants at all
Because the ground stays frozen all year
questions.answer: The great diversity of plants gives them lots of food and shelter
questions.hint: Plants provide leaves, fruits, branches, and hiding spots!
questions.explanation: The great diversity of plants in a rainforest provides food and shelter for many kinds of animals!

questions.instruction: Identify Temperate Forest animals.
questions.text: Which animals might you see in a temperate forest?
questions.answer: Squirrels, raccoons, bears, and deer
questions.hint: Remember our slide with the cute bear climbing a trunk and two squirrels holding an acorn!
questions.explanation: Temperate forests may have squirrels, raccoons, bears, deer, and many types of birds!

questions.instruction: Find the bird home in a Temperate Forest.
questions.text: What part of trees in a temperate forest provides shelter for many types of birds?
questions.answer: Hollows in trees
questions.hint: Look at the woodpecker beside the round opening in the tree trunk!
questions.explanation: Hollows in temperate forest trees provide cozy shelter for many types of birds!

questions.instruction: Describe the Tundra climate.
questions.text: Which sentence describes a tundra habitat?
options: It is cold all year round, often windy, and gets very little rain
It is hot and humid with tall tropical ferns
It is flooded with warm water every month
It has giant palm trees on sandy beaches
questions.answer: It is cold all year round, often windy, and gets very little rain
questions.hint: Snowflakes and wind are in our Tundra picture!
questions.explanation: A tundra habitat is cold all year round with very little rain and is often windy!

questions.instruction: Remember the origin of the word 'tundra'.
questions.text: The word 'tundra' comes from the Finnish word 'tunturi', which means ___.
questions.answer: treeless plain
questions.hint: Few trees can grow in the cold, windy tundra!
questions.explanation: Tundra comes from the Finnish word 'tunturi', meaning 'treeless plain'!

questions.instruction: Think about plants in the Tundra.
questions.text: During the warmer spring and summer months in a tundra, what do many small shrubs produce?
questions.answer: Colorful wildflowers
questions.hint: Look at the bottom of the Tundra card showing purple, yellow, and pink blooms peeking through snow!
questions.explanation: When spring and summer warm up the tundra, many shrubs produce colorful wildflowers!

questions.instruction: Notice what plants mostly grow in the Tundra.
questions.text: Why do FEW trees grow in tundras, while most plants are grasses or small shrubs?
options: Because the tundra stays cold, windy, and snowy/icy most of the year
Because tundras get too much sunlight and rain
Because giraffes eat all the tundra trees
questions.answer: Because the tundra stays cold, windy, and snowy/icy most of the year
questions.hint: Frozen icy ground and cold winds make it hard for big trees to grow!
questions.explanation: Because a tundra is cold, windy, and icy for most of the year, few trees grow there — mostly grasses and small shrubs!

questions.instruction: Identify Tundra animals.
questions.text: Which animals are adapted to live in the tundra?
options: Polar bears, reindeer, foxes, and hares
questions.answer: Polar bears, reindeer, foxes, and hares
questions.hint: Look at the polar bear, bunny hare, reindeer, and fox near the igloo on our Tundra Fauna card!
questions.explanation: Polar bears, reindeer, foxes, and hares are tundra animals!

questions.instruction: Understand Tundra winter survival.
questions.text: During freezing winters, what do many tundra animals do?
options: Move underground to stay warm or move to warmer places
Climb to the tops of tall rainforest trees
Drink salt water from the ocean
Stand on top of open ocean waves
questions.answer: Move underground to stay warm or move to warmer places
questions.hint: How can an animal escape the icy winter wind?
questions.explanation: During winter, many tundra animals burrow underground to stay warm or travel to warmer places!

questions.instruction: Compare Tropical Rainforest vs. Tundra.
questions.text: Which statement correctly compares a Tropical Rainforest and a Tundra?
options: A rainforest is warm with lots of rain and diverse plants; a tundra is cold with few trees
A tundra has tall leafy palm trees; a rainforest is covered in ice
Neither habitat has any animals at all
questions.answer: A rainforest is warm with lots of rain and diverse plants; a tundra is cold with few trees
questions.hint: Contrast warm & rainy vs. cold & snowy!
questions.explanation: Rainforests are warm, rainy, and full of diverse trees and animals, while tundras are cold with few trees!

questions.instruction: Classify Ponds and Lakes.
questions.text: Ponds and lakes are ___ freshwater habitats.
questions.answer: closed
questions.hint: Unlike a flowing river, pond water stays enclosed in one basin!
questions.explanation: Ponds and lakes are closed freshwater habitats!

questions.instruction: Notice where plants grow in Ponds and Lakes.
questions.text: In pond and lake habitats, where can plants grow?
options: In the surrounding land, ON the water, and UNDER the water
Only in salt water far out at sea
questions.answer: In the surrounding land, ON the water, and UNDER the water
questions.hint: Think of cattails on the bank, lily pads on top, and waterweeds underwater!
questions.explanation: Pond and lake plants live in the land around water, floating on the water, and underwater too — and flowers attract insects!

questions.instruction: Spot animals of Ponds and Lakes.
questions.text: Which animals are common in pond and lake habitats?
options: Turtles, frogs, birds, and reptiles like lizards and snakes
questions.answer: Turtles, frogs, birds, and reptiles like lizards and snakes
questions.hint: Remember the green turtle and dragonfly card for Activity 3.8!
questions.explanation: Ponds and lakes are home to turtles, frogs, birds, and reptiles such as lizards and snakes!

questions.instruction: Compare Rivers/Streams to Ponds/Lakes.
questions.text: How is the water in a river or stream DIFFERENT from a closed pond?
options: The freshwater in a river moves from one place to another
A river has salt water while oceans have fresh water
A river never contains any water
Rivers only flow inside deserts without plants
questions.answer: The freshwater in a river moves from one place to another
questions.hint: Think of water flowing downstream!
questions.explanation: Rivers and streams are freshwater habitats where the water moves from one place to another!

questions.instruction: Think about plants near Rivers and Streams.
questions.text: How do trees, large shrubs, and grasses around rivers and streams get water?
options: Their roots take in water from the wet soil
They swim inside the river with fins
They catch snowflakes in their petals
questions.answer: Their roots take in water from the wet soil
questions.hint: The riverbank soil stays damp from the moving water!
questions.explanation: Trees, large shrubs, and grasses grow around rivers and streams because their roots take in water from the wet soil!

questions.instruction: Remember this Amazing Fact from the Rivers card!
questions.text: What special animal lives in the freshwater rivers and streams of the Amazon river?
questions.answer: The Amazon river dolphin
questions.hint: Most dolphins live in saltwater oceans, except this special freshwater pink dolphin!
questions.explanation: The Amazon river dolphin is a special dolphin species that lives in freshwater rivers and streams!

questions.instruction: Define a Wetland habitat.
questions.text: What makes a habitat a WETLAND?
options: Land that is flooded with water for all or most of the year
Land that never sees a drop of rain
A frozen iceberg in the middle of the ocean
A dry tropical grassland with lions
questions.answer: Land that is flooded with water for all or most of the year
questions.hint: Look right inside the word: WET + LAND!
questions.explanation: A wetland is a habitat that is flooded with water for all or most of the year!

questions.instruction: Check what kind of water Wetlands can have.
questions.text: Which statement about water in wetlands is TRUE?
options: Some wetlands have fresh water and some have salt water
All wetlands can only ever have frozen snow
Wetlands have zero water at any time
questions.answer: Some wetlands have fresh water and some have salt water
questions.hint: Think: inland wetlands vs. coastal wetlands near the sea!
questions.explanation: Some wetlands have fresh water, and wetlands near the ocean can have salt water!

questions.instruction: Answer the Wetland Cloud Question!
questions.text: What happens when the amount of water in a wetland changes or dries up for a while?
options: Plants and animals change too — plants grow back and animals return or come out when water returns
Cactuses instantly grow into oak trees
Nothing in nature ever notices water changes
questions.answer: Plants and animals change too — plants grow back and animals return or come out when water returns
questions.hint: Remember our Wetlands card: some plants die in dry times and grow back when water returns, and animals adapt or move!
questions.explanation: As water in a wetland changes, plants and animals change too: plants grow back when water returns, and animals move to wet spots or shelter in mud until water comes back!

questions.instruction: Spot Wetland animals.
questions.text: What kinds of animals live in a wetland habitat?
options: A huge variety: insects, fish, amphibians, reptiles, and mammals
questions.answer: A huge variety: insects, fish, amphibians, reptiles, and mammals
questions.hint: Remember the capybara family with little fish and lily pads on Activity 3.10!
questions.explanation: Wetlands hold a great variety of insects, fish, amphibians, reptiles, and mammals!

questions.instruction: Identify the largest habitat on Earth.
questions.text: Which habitat is the LARGEST habitat on Earth and covers most of Earth's surface?
questions.answer: Oceans
questions.hint: Look at a blue globe of Earth — most of it is covered in huge salt water!
questions.explanation: Oceans are huge bodies of salt water and are the largest habitat on Earth!

questions.instruction: Compare Oceans with Rivers and Lakes.
questions.text: How are ocean habitats DIFFERENT from lakes and rivers?
options: Oceans have salty water and cover most of Earth, while lakes and rivers have fresh water
Lakes and rivers have salt water, while oceans are completely dry
Oceans are closed tiny puddles in a garden
There is no difference between oceans and ponds
questions.answer: Oceans have salty water and cover most of Earth, while lakes and rivers have fresh water
questions.hint: Think: fresh water vs. salt water, and size!
questions.explanation: Oceans are vast bodies of salt water covering most of Earth, whereas lakes and rivers are smaller freshwater habitats!

questions.instruction: Compare shallow vs. deep ocean habitats.
questions.text: How can two parts of the ocean be different from each other?
options: Shallow ocean habitats have warm water, while deep ocean habitats are cold all year round
Deep ocean water is dry sand, while shallow water is frozen solid
Every inch of the ocean has the exact same warmth
Only plants live in the ocean, never animals
questions.answer: Shallow ocean habitats have warm water, while deep ocean habitats are cold all year round
questions.hint: Does sunlight reach deep down to the bottom of the ocean?
questions.explanation: Shallow ocean parts are warm from sunlight, while deep ocean habitats stay cold all year round — and different animals live in different parts!

questions.instruction: Check Activity 3.11: How do fish breathe?
questions.text: Fish, like most ocean animals, have ___ to get the air they need directly from water.
questions.answer: gills
questions.hint: Fish do NOT have to swim to the surface to gulp air — look at the slits on their sides!
questions.explanation: Most ocean animals, like fish, have gills to get the air they need from water!

questions.instruction: Check Activity 3.11: How do ocean mammals & turtles breathe?
questions.text: Dolphins, whales, and sea turtles come up to the ocean surface to breathe in air because they have ___.
questions.answer: lungs
questions.hint: Think of a dolphin jumping or blowing air from its blowhole at the surface!
questions.explanation: Ocean animals like dolphins, whales, and turtles have lungs and come up to the surface to breathe air!
